subject: Follow-up: Ledgerly inference budget gap, batching & cache levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Sam Black <sam.black@ledgerly.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Ledgerly inference budget gap, batching & cache levers

Hi Sophie / Sam —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap from our side so we’re all aligned, and a concrete set of next steps so your finance and engineering teams can evaluate the pilot.

Pain points you shared
- Current latency spikes on nightly reconciliation jobs when throughput surges (25–30% of run time).
- Token cost is the single line-item pushing the project over the fiscal Q3 approval threshold (~$45k/month target).
- Security constraints require data routing in a VPC and audit logs retained for 90 days.

Goals we heard
- Run a 6–8 week pilot that shows 40–60% unit-cost reduction vs your current setup while maintaining sub-250ms median token latency for interactive flows.
- Keep pilot spend under $20k total committed budget (finance constraint).

Options & levers we propose (high level)
1) Batching profile: move reconciliation batch windows to a continuous-batch runner we configure — estimated 20–35% token-cost reduction for reconciliation workloads.
2) Prefix / KV caching: short-lived KV caching for recent user contexts — expected 10–25% savings on interactive calls where repetition is high.
3) Model quantization: recommend 4-bit quantized variant for higher-throughput routes; small quality trade-offs on long multi-turn prompts.
4) Routing policy: split low-priority background jobs to cheaper instance types with burst capacity for spikes.

Preliminary economics (very rough)
- Baseline: current average cost estimate from your team = $0.18 / 1k tokens for the workload shapes shared.
- With batching + caching + quantization, model-level blended estimate = ~$0.06–0.10 / 1k tokens; pilot-level savings target = 45%–60% depending on traffic mix.

Ask / next steps
- Sophie / finance: can you confirm the hard pilot budget cap and whether a $10k refundable pilot deposit is acceptable for a reserved short-duration pool?
- Sophie / Sam: please share (or point to) a small sample query set (10–50 representative requests) and an S3 path to historical reconciliation job logs so we can run an internal cost simulation.
- Internal: Monica, Aditya — can you prepare a brief SOW draft and a pricing matrix showing both hosted and dedicated pilot options? I attached a first-pass matrix and SOW.

I’ll hold on building a production rollout plan until we lock the budget and sample data. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min technical review next week with infra/eng.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-inference-pricing-matrix.xlsx, ledgerly-pilot-sow-draft.pdf
From: Sophie Park <sophie@ledgerly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Black <sam.black@ledgerly.com>, finance@ledgerly.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Ledgerly inference budget gap, batching & cache levers

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Budget constraint: finance confirmed we have $20k approved for vendor evaluation in Q3 but it must be consumed within the quarter. We can do a refundable deposit up to $7k — not $10k.
2) Security: we need VPC + KMS + audit stream to our Splunk instance; 90-day retention is required. We’ll need that in the SOW.
3) Data sample: Sam will drop a sanitized S3 path by end of day tomorrow. The reconciliation jobs are mostly batch jobs that spike at EOD UTC.

Tradeoffs: We’re OK testing a quantized model for background reconciliation but need higher fidelity for customer-facing interactive flows. If caching reduces cost for interactive flows without harming perceived correctness, that’s ideal.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- Revised SOW that includes security controls (VPC + KMS + Splunk forwarder) and a pilot timeline that fits within the quarter.
- A cost-sim using our sample logs (once Sam shares).

Sophie
Head of ML, Ledgerly
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@ledgerly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Ledgerly inference budget gap, batching & cache levers

Sophie — quick note from pricing/ops: we can accept a $7k refundable deposit for the pilot. Two optional commercial levers to keep tracker-friendly pricing under $20k:

A) Pilot constrained reserved pool: we can reserve a small dedicated pool (4–8 GPUs depending on throughput) for the 6-week pilot and cap spend at $18k. This gives stable latency and predictable unit costs for the evaluation.

B) Consumption + credit model: hosted pilot where Ledgerly pays consumption up to $15k and Redwood provides $5k in pilot credit that phases out if you convert to a 12-month reserved capacity within 60 days.

We’ll add security language around VPC and KMS in the SOW draft. Monica — can you fold the deposit terms and the two commercial options into the SOW and return both an engineering and a legal-ready version?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Manager, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround, everyone. Action items I’ll own:
- Update SOW with security clauses + two commercial options (Aditya / Monica to review internal).
- Run a preliminary cost sim using Ledgerly sample once Sam shares (I’ll track this with you, Sophie).
- Schedule a 30-min technical sync for Tues next week (I'll propose time via calendar invite).

Sophie / Sam: if you can confirm S3 path and finance acceptance of the $7k deposit, we’ll move to SOW review and a start date for the pilot.

Marissa
